task.description:
WF-03 Step 5 (close the issue) for ISS-0119.

THE STATUS DECISION IS YOURS AND IT IS NOT A FORMALITY. `docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md`'s 'Issue status vocabulary' section is canonical -- read it before deciding. `resolved` asserts that A ROOT CAUSE WAS ACTUALLY REMOVED and a regression test proves it; shipping useful verified work is explicitly NOT the same thing. `instrumented` is for a run that built and verified real improvements but did NOT remove the root cause, and it REQUIRES a `superseded_by:` pointer. This project has a live worked example of the distinction going the other way: ISS-0109, from the immediately preceding run, was transitioned to `instrumented` with `superseded_by: ISS-0116` because its design gate and REVIEWER independently concluded the failure was instrumented, not fixed. Do not pattern-match to that precedent; decide ISS-0119 on its own facts.

DECIDE BY RE-DERIVING, NOT BY READING THIS HANDOFF. ISS-0119's own words state the defect: the file outgrew the 256KB read limit, so 'the instruction every agent is given before touching that file -- read the existing file in full before touching it, preserve its established schema, append, never rewrite -- is no longer literally executable by any agent in this pipeline', and the safeguard's mechanism (see the whole file -> notice the schema -> append rather than invent) was broken while the instruction depending on it stayed written down and apparently followed. It also names a second gap (the `req: SCOPE-CHANGE` convention documented nowhere) and forbids one resolution route outright: 'Do not resolve this by relaxing the append-only rule. The rule is correct; the mechanism supporting it has degraded.'

So the questions you must answer for yourself, against the tree as it now stands:
  - Is the current volume actually readable in one call now? Measure it.
  - Does the header prescribe a procedure an agent can actually execute, on both shells this project uses?
  - Is the full history preserved with nothing dropped, and is that mechanically enforced rather than merely intended?
  - Was the append-only rule relaxed anywhere? (If it was, that alone forbids `resolved`.)
  - Is the `req:`/`event:` vocabulary now documented where an appending agent lands?
  - Does a regression test prove it, and was that test shown to fail before the fix and pass after?
Then state the verdict with the evidence, and set `status:` accordingly. If you conclude `instrumented`, you MUST file the successor first and record `superseded_by:` -- report that to ORCH rather than filing it yourself.

BE HONEST ABOUT WHAT WAS NOT CLOSED. Whatever verdict you reach, the record must not overstate it. Known boundaries, established by this run's own gates and not to be quietly dropped:
  - TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR recorded that remedy (b) is asserted at TOKEN LEVEL ONLY -- A8 checks the header contains the required tokens; it cannot assert the HOW-TO-APPEND prose is genuinely executable, because prose executability is not mechanically assertable by a unit test.
  - The `TASK_QUEUE.md:133` instruction defect that CAUSED the three `event: SCOPE-CHANGE` anomalies is corrected as a doc edit with no assertion behind it. A4a asserts the DATA, never the INSTRUCTION, so a future edit could reintroduce the wrong-field convention and A4a would only notice after entries were written under it.
  - The three malformed entries in frozen volume 1 are DECLARED, not corrected -- and by design can never be corrected, since volume 1 is frozen and A6-pinned.
  - ISS-0193 (queue task 193, GH#381) was filed by this run for the same declare-to-silence hole surviving in `known_anomalies:`/A5, plus the roll-boundary variant. Cross-reference it.

IF YOU SET `resolved`: also set `resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0119-20260821` and `resolved_at:` from a REAL clock reading (`date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"`), and close the GitHub issue named in the record's `github_issue:` field (#373) with `gh issue close 373 --comment "Fixed in WF03-ISS0119-20260821. See docs/issues/ISS-0119.yaml and the regression test at test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs."`. Note the record's `queue_task_id:` is 186 -- ORCH releases that lock itself, do not call the queue.

Do not edit anything under docs/status/, any test file, or the design artefact. Your write scope is docs/issues/ plus your own handoff. handoffs/orchestrator.log has uncommitted ORCH edits and docs/issues/ISS-0193.yaml is a new untracked ORCH file -- leave BOTH alone and do not commit them. Stage by explicit path, never `git add -A`.
acceptance_criteria: ISSUE_QUEUE.md's status vocabulary was read and the resolved-vs-instrumented choice is justified against its definitions, not by precedent
The verdict is re-derived from the tree as it stands, with each of the six questions answered on evidence the agent generated or read directly
docs/issues/ISS-0119.yaml carries the chosen status, and if resolved, resolved_in_run and a real-clock resolved_at
If instrumented, a successor is reported to ORCH and superseded_by is recorded -- an instrumented record is never a dead end
The record states plainly what was NOT closed, covering the four known boundaries listed in this handoff
If resolved, GitHub issue #373 was closed with the specified comment, or the failure to do so is recorded explicitly
No file outside docs/issues/ and this handoff was modified

result.summary: VERDICT: resolved -- not instrumented. Decided against ISSUE_QUEUE.md's definitions, not against the ISS-0109 precedent. `resolved` requires that a root cause was ACTUALLY REMOVED and that a regression test proves it. ISS-0119's root cause is stated in its own words: the instruction 'read the existing file in full before touching it ... append, never rewrite' had become unexecutable, because the file agents must read before appending exceeded the Read tool's limit. That is a mechanism defect with a physical bound, and the bound is now met on the file agents actually append to. That is removal, not instrumentation -- which is exactly what separates this from ISS-0109, where the root cause remained unknown and only diagnostics shipped. All six questions were re-derived at Step 5 from the tree, generating the evidence here rather than reading upstream summaries. (1) READABLE: current volume docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml = 140 lines / 7,994 bytes; index = 165 lines / 7,884 bytes (wc -l/wc -c on the working tree). Both far inside 262,144 bytes / 2,000 lines, and both were read in full, unscoped, in this step. (2) PROCEDURE EXECUTABLE ON BOTH SHELLS: I ran the v2 header's step-1 one-liners as written -- `grep -n 'status: current' -B 2 <index>` under Bash and `Select-String -Path <index> -Pattern 'status: current' -Context 2,0` under PowerShell. Both printed the `- volume: 2` / `path:` pair above the marker, resolving the append target correctly. The step-2 measurement pairs and step-3 clock pairs were run on both shells too (PowerShell clock returned 2026-08-21T08:56:14Z). (3) HISTORY PRESERVED, MECHANICALLY: volume 1 frozen in place, not split or renamed -- all 182 entries intact (grep -c '^  - req:' = 182), and the ~103 run records citing that path plus the by-line citation at iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367 stay valid. I recomputed the frozen-prefix digest independently of the suite (head -5766, CRLF->LF, sha256) = 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804, matching the index exactly; A6 asserts it on every run. (4) APPEND-ONLY NOT RELAXED -- checked directly because relaxation alone would forbid `resolved`. `git diff main...HEAD` over anti-patterns.md, core-directives.md, TASK_QUEUE.md, doc-updater.md, release-validator.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENT_SYSTEM.md and WF-02 shows the rule STRENGTHENED everywhere it is restated: it now binds 'in this volume or any closed one', adds a `git diff --numstat` deletions-must-be-zero step, and core-directives item 3 now settles the precedence ISS-0119 said nothing recorded (scoped reads govern closed volumes; the current volume is the single full-read exception, and only because the roll rule makes that read executable). No edit anywhere permits partial-read-then-append. (5) VOCABULARY DOCUMENTED WHERE AN APPENDER LANDS: v2's header carries both complete lists -- `req:` has exactly two legal values and names `req: ISS-NNNN` as the wrong guess with zero precedent; `event:` has six, correcting volume 1's own header which listed three while three more were in use. The causing instruction at TASK_QUEUE.md:133 is corrected to name the field. (6) REGRESSION TEST, SHOWN RED FIRST: A3 resolves the volume and its ceilings through the index (hardcoding neither, which is what makes it directional). It was run in a throwaway worktree at pre-fix commit 3d19e8c and failed on SIZE (over: [:lines, :bytes], 4,217 lines / 264,861 bytes), then passed unmodified on the fix branch. I re-ran it myself at Step 5: `mix test test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs` -> '13 passed', 0.4s. TEST-RUNNER separately had all 13 green in full-suite context in both branch runs. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, recorded verbatim in the record's new `not_closed_by_this_run:` block so the registry does not overstate the fix: (a) remedy (b) is asserted at TOKEN LEVEL ONLY -- A8 checks the header contains the required tokens and that its ceilings match the index, and cannot assert the HOW-TO-APPEND prose is executable; my both-shells run above is a one-time check, not a standing assertion. (b) The TASK_QUEUE.md:133 instruction fix has no assertion behind it -- A4a asserts the DATA, never the INSTRUCTION, so a reintroduced wrong-field convention would only be caught after entries were written under it. (c) The three malformed volume-1 entries (3490/REQ-031, 3577/REQ-042, 3744/REQ-038) are DECLARED, not corrected, and by design can never be corrected -- volume 1 is frozen and A6-pinned; same for the three shape anomalies A4 found on its first run (4803, 4896, 5050), on disk undetected since 2026-08-19. (d) The declare-to-silence hole survives in `known_anomalies:`/A5 -- A4b got the closed-and-pinned rule, A5 did not, and the roll-boundary variant remains; carried by ISS-0193 (queue task 193, GH#381), cross-referenced in the record's `see_also:`. That residue is bounded and separately tracked, and is not part of ISS-0119's own root cause, which is why it does not hold this record open. ONE DISTINCTION DELIBERATELY NOT BLURRED, also written into the record: remedy (a) as worded said 'make the file readable again'. Volume 1 itself is STILL 363,951 bytes and a whole-file read of it is still refused. What changed is that no instruction asks for one -- it is closed, frozen, off the append path, targeted-read only. The safeguard's mechanism is restored on the file agents append to, which is what the defect was about. ACTIONS: docs/issues/ISS-0119.yaml set to `resolved` with resolved_in_run and a real-clock resolved_at (2026-08-21T08:57:06Z, `date -u`), plus `resolution:`, `not_closed_by_this_run:`, `see_also: [ISS-0193]` and `resolution_artifacts:`; YAML re-parsed clean. GH#373 closed with the specified comment ('Closed issue tvolodi/letflow#373'). No `superseded_by:` -- that field is required for `instrumented` only. Queue task 186 NOT touched; ORCH releases it. Nothing outside docs/issues/ISS-0119.yaml and this handoff was modified: handoffs/orchestrator.log and the untracked docs/issues/ISS-0193.yaml were left alone and not staged. SCHEMA CORRECTION (post-review, this file only): the envelope `status` was first written as "COMPLETE", which is not one of the six values HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:55 defines (PENDING|IN_PROGRESS|COMPLETED|FAILED|ESCALATED|CANCELLED); corrected to "COMPLETED", as :210 also directs. Both sets were re-checked against the protocol directly rather than taken on report: `result.status` draws from a different five-value set at :72 (PASS|FAIL|PARTIAL|BLOCKED|SKIPPED) and PASS was already legal. This is the second envelope-value slip in this run (CODE-DESIGNER's "SUCCESS" was the first), which is itself worth recording -- :269's Enforcement note reports unenforced bookkeeping rules being complied with at 0.4-8.6%, and with no handoff linter in Letflow yet, conformance holds only where an agent notices. Nothing else in this handoff or in docs/issues/ISS-0119.yaml was changed.
result.next_action: ORCH: release queue task 186 with status 'done' (GH#373 is already closed), then proceed to Step Final (git-merge). No successor issue is required for ISS-0119 itself; ISS-0193/GH#381 already carries the residual declare-to-silence work and is cross-referenced from the record.
